nodes.description: Needle-like opacities, associated with the R58H allele in several unrelated families and with P23T in an Indian family; one R58H family member had a coral-like cataract instead.

evidence.reference_title: The gamma-crystallins and human cataracts: a puzzle made clearer.
evidence.snippet: We recently mapped the aculeiform cataract to the gamma-crystallin locus (CRYG) on chromosome 2q33-35, and mutational analysis of the CRYG-genes cluster identified the aculeiform-cataract mutation in exon 2 of gamma-crystallin D (CRYGD).

evidence.reference_title: CRYGD gene analysis in a family with autosomal dominant congenital cataract: evidence for molecular homogeneity and intrafamilial clinical heterogeneity in aculeiform cataract.
evidence.snippet: The R58H mutation described in this Mexican family is identical to that demonstrated previously in three unrelated families with aculeiform cataract, suggesting that this type of cataract has a specific molecular basis represented by the Arg to His change at residue 58 of CRYGD.

evidence.reference_title: A missense mutation in CRYGD linked with autosomal dominant congenital cataract of aculeiform type.
evidence.snippet: The present study describes identification of p.Pro23Thr mutation in CRYGD for aculeiform type cataract in an ADCC family of Indian origin.

nodes.description: Reported in all affected members of the W43R family.

evidence.reference_title: Progressive juvenile-onset punctate cataracts caused by mutation of the gammaD-crystallin gene.

evidence.reference_title: Gamma-D crystallin gene (CRYGD) mutation causes autosomal dominant congenital cerulean cataracts.
evidence.snippet: The maximum lod score (7.19 at recombination fraction theta=0) was obtained for marker D2S2208 near the gamma-crystallin gene (CRYG) cluster.

evidence.reference_title: Investigation of crystallin genes in familial cataract, and report of two disease associated mutations.
evidence.snippet: Sequencing revealed a P23T mutation of CRYGD, found to segregate with disease.

evidence.reference_title: Mutational spectrum in a Chinese cohort with congenital cataracts.
evidence.snippet: 27.37% of variants (23/84) were commonly detected in PAX6, GJA8 and CRYGD, and the three genes covered 33.06% of cases (41/124) with molecular diagnosis.

evidence.reference_title: Evaluating gene-disease relationship strength in crystallin genes in association with pediatric cataracts.
evidence.snippet: Seven genes (CRYAA, CRYAB, CRYBA1, CRYBB1, CRYBB2, CRYGC, CRYGD) scored as Definitively associated with autosomal dominant (AD) inherited pediatric cataracts.

nodes.description: Heterozygous missense, nonsense and frameshift variants in CRYGD. Most pathogenic missense alleles change surface residues (R14C, P23T, R36S, R58H, E107A); others change structurally critical residues (W43R) or truncate the C-terminal Greek key motifs (W156X, Y134X, and frameshifts). The biophysical studies below attribute the cataract to properties gained by the mutant protein. One allele points the other way: in transfected cells R36P lowers the total and soluble amount of gamma-D crystallin without increasing the insoluble fraction, so a reduced soluble pool may contribute for some alleles; this has not been tested in lens.

evidence.reference_title: Progressive juvenile-onset punctate cataracts caused by mutation of the gammaD-crystallin gene.
evidence.snippet: A single base alteration resulting in an Arg- 14 --> Cys (R14C) substitution in gammaD-crystallin was subsequently identified.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital coralliform cataract is the predominant consequence of a recurrent mutation in the CRYGD gene.
evidence.snippet: The solubility and stability of γD-crystallin is indispensable for the lens transparency. Mutation in CRYGD gene may destroy the solubility and stability of the crystallin proteins, subsequently reduce lens transparency causing CC.

evidence.reference_title: Link between a novel human gammaD-crystallin allele and a unique cataract phenotype explained by protein crystallography.
evidence.snippet: Sequencing of the CRYGD gene has shown a heterozygous C-->A transversion in position 109 of the inferred cDNA (36R-->S transversion of the processed, N-terminal methionine-lacking CRYGD).

evidence.reference_title: A missense mutation in the gammaD crystallin gene (CRYGD) associated with autosomal dominant "coral-like" cataract linked to chromosome 2q.
evidence.snippet: Sequencing of the CRYGA-CRYGD cluster identified a C->A transversion in exon 2 of CRYGD that was predicted to result in the non-conservative substitution of threonine for proline at amino-acid residue 23 (P23T) in the processed CRYGD protein.

evidence.reference_title: A novel CRYGD mutation (p.Trp43Arg) causing autosomal dominant congenital cataract in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: This mutation co-segregated with all affected individuals and was not observed in either unaffected family members or in 200 normal unrelated individuals.

evidence.reference_title: A potential novel role of the R36P mutation in CRYGD in congenial cataract.
evidence.snippet: The total protein, especially the soluble fraction, was significantly reduced in the R36P mutant, while the insoluble part remained unaffected.

nodes.description: Lens extraction is the standard management of visually significant CRYGD cataract, performed from early infancy for dense congenital opacities and in childhood or adolescence for the progressive R14C cataract. In paediatric cataract generally it is lens aspiration with or without intraocular lens implantation, followed by amblyopia therapy, and for dense bilateral congenital cataract the timing of surgery in the first weeks of life governs visual outcome. The timing and technique evidence comes from cohorts that were not genotyped. Complications after paediatric cataract surgery include secondary membranes over the visual axis requiring re-operation and glaucoma, both more frequent after surgery in the first four weeks of life. No CRYGD-specific therapy exists.

evidence.reference_title: Progressive juvenile-onset punctate cataracts caused by mutation of the gammaD-crystallin gene.
evidence.snippet: The opacification evolves relatively slowly, generally necessitating removal of the lens in childhood or early adolescence.

evidence.reference_title: A novel CRYGD mutation (p.Trp43Arg) causing autosomal dominant congenital cataract in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: All patients had undergone cataract extraction during childhood.

evidence.snippet: Their father and 2 older brothers, all of whom underwent childhood cataract surgery, also harbored the mutation while the 2 asymptomatic immediate family members did not.

evidence.snippet: At position 58, the mutant protein loses the direct ion-pair intermolecular interaction present in the wild-type, due to the differences between histidine and arginine at the atomic level; the interaction in the mutant is mediated by water molecules.

nodes.description: A second group of alleles does perturb the protein. W43R (W42R in processed-protein numbering) lowers stability, and in vitro the W42R mutant aggregates through a non-native internal disulfide that locks a misfolded, aggregation-prone intermediate. C-terminal truncations (W156X, Y151X, T160RfsX8) disrupt Greek key motif 4, destabilize the protein and expose hydrophobic side chains to solvent. In cultured cells heat, UV and oxidative stress increase aggregation of truncated mutants, and co-expressed alpha-crystallins reduce it.

nodes.description: For R14C, P23T, R36S, R58H and E107A the recombinant mutant protein has essentially the secondary structure, tertiary structure and conformational stability of wild type. What changes is its intermolecular behavior: an extra exposed cysteine (R14C), a solubility that falls as temperature rises (P23T), or loss of the arginine side chain whose absence allows crystal packing (R36S) or removes an intermolecular ion pair (R58H). These alleles showed that unfolding is not required for a crystallin to cause cataract.
